name: 21-heal-at-mt-moon
objective: Up Route 4's southern spur to the Mt Moon Pokemon Center, and heal at the counter, before going into the mountain.
evidence: map=0x44 - wCurMap $D35E. MT_MOON_POKECENTER is const index 68, and Route 4's own object data names it: map $0F's warp[0] at (11,5) leads to map $44 warp[0], and map $44 decodes as tileset 6, 14x8 blocks with warps at (3,7) and (4,7) back to $FF - the same building as Viridian's $29 and Pewter's $3A, tile for tile, which is why one waypoint list serves all three.

watch:last_blackout_map=0x0F - wLastBlackoutMap $D719, and THE VALUE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, the same way link 16's $02 was. On the certified link-20 exit pool it reads $02 (Pewter City, where the chain last healed) on every one of 598 states; on this link's own exits it reads $0F on every one of 120. So the byte holds the map the Centre was entered from - Route 4 - and not the Centre's own $44, exactly as Pewter's holds the town and not $3A. The cartridge writes it in DisplayPokemonCenterDialogue's call to SetLastBlackoutMap.

party_missing_hp=0 AND map=0x44 are both needed beside the flip, for the reasons link 16 measured on the same building: $D719 is written at the START of the nurse's dialogue, before HealParty runs, so the flip alone proves the conversation began rather than that the party is whole; and finishing INSIDE the building is what forces anyone hurt through the nurse instead of being satisfied by walking past the door.

THE ENTRY POINT IS (9,17) ON ROUTE 4 AND IS DERIVED BEFORE IT IS OBSERVED. Route 3's north connection carries yalign 17 and xalign 206 (= -50), so leaving Route 3 at (59,0) arrives at Route 4 (9,17); measured on all 598 link-20 exits, x=0x09 y=0x11. Route 4's own south connection says the same in reverse, yalign 0 and xalign 50.

There are three doors on row 5 and only two of them are reachable from here: (11,5) the Pokemon Center and (18,5) the mountain's west mouth. (24,5) is the mouth Mt Moon puts you back out of, and x=20-23 is solid on rows 6, 7 and 8, so it cannot be walked to from this side. Mt Moon is not a shortcut round Route 4; it is the only way east.
